can_do_statement: Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to combine phrases.

ontology.mental_model: Structuring parallel parts of speech or phrases into a unified communicative whole.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use simple linkers to connect related phrases side-by-side.

positives: The kitchen is quite large and brightly lit.
She likes to go to the cinema or to the theatre.
negatives: And I went home.
He came in and sat down.

example_raw:
My home is very light and very comfortable. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Polish; Pass)

I live with my mother and her boyfriend. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Polish; Pass)

My house is small but very nice. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Pashto; Pass)

She likes to go to the cinema or to the theatre. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; French; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to combine sentences.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Start a new sentence with 'And', 'But', or 'Or' to carry forward the previous idea.

positives: He is very clever. But he never studies.
And then we went to the market.
negatives: I like apples and oranges.
They can either stay here or go home.

example_raw:
I like it because there are lots of shops, it is not too busy and there is lots of parking. And I like my home because it's not too big and it's a very nice flat. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Tamil; Pass)

I am from Estonia. Estonia it is a small country near the Baltic Sea. But now I live in Dorchester, because I work here. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Russian; Pass)

I go shopping on Ladypool Road. Or sometimes I go to my local shop.  (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Panjabi; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use 'and' and 'or' before the final item in a list.

ontology.mental_model: Organizing sequential items before concluding a list.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use a comma for the first items, and save the linker for the very last item.

positives: I bought milk, bread, and cheese.
We can visit Paris, Rome, or Madrid.
negatives: He sings and dances.
I don't know if he came or went.

example_raw:
I like to eat chicken, mushrooms and some vegetables. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Polish; Pass)

I have three rooms; a kitchen, living room, bathroom and toilet. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Polish; Pass)

I go to college every Tuesday, Thursday and Friday morning, (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; French; Pass)

I really like my English course because there are very good students from other countries, for example from Italy, Portugal, China and India. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Slovak; Pass)
I like to eat steak, vegetables, potatoes or rice. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Polish; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to combine clauses.

ontology.mental_model: Integrating distinct actions or states into a single complex sentence.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use these words to glue two complete mini-sentences together.

positives: He is a doctor, and he works very hard.
She didn't like the food, but she ate it anyway.
negatives: I want a burger and fries.
The tall but ugly building.

example_raw:
He is a journalist and he likes everything about cinema. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Italian; Pass)

There are lots of shops in the town and the town is only five minutes away. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Urdu; Pass)

I have visited a lot of places, but the best place is Thailand. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Slovak; Pass)

I like to eat pasta or pizza, but I'm easy about food, I can eat anything. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; French; Pass)

We love to go to the cinema, or just sit together and have a laugh. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Portuguese; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to connect single nouns and adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: Pairing basic vocabulary words directly together.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Connect two nouns or two adjectives simply with 'and', 'but', or 'or'.

positives: The cat is black and white.
Do you want tea or coffee?
negatives: He came in and sat down.
And I agree with you.

example_raw:
I like chicken and rice. I don't like meat and fish. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Kurdish; Pass)

My street is quiet and friendly. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Polish; Pass)

On Monday and Wednesday I have English and maths. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Polish; Pass)

I like my kitchen, it is small but nice. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Polish; Pass)

I like cheese pizza or chicken. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; French; Pass)

I like to eat soup, eggs, meat and salad or banana and cheese. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Polish; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use 'either … or' to connect two words, phrases or clauses.

ontology.mental_model: Framing an exclusive choice between two alternatives.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'either' to introduce a choice, and 'or' for the second option.

positives: You can have either cake or ice cream.
We will either walk or take the bus.
negatives: I don't like it either.
Did you see him or her?

example_raw:
The men wear suits, either white or black, and the bride and women wear special long dresses, usually the same colour. (Yugoslavia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Serbian; Pass)

We can go either to the beach or to the inner part of Uruguay which is mainly a huge meadow. (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I'll either write or phone you soon. (Japan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Japanese; Pass)

You can either go to the gym or attend some special classes, where you do gentle exercises. (Ukraine; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Ukrainian; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use 'but' to add an unexpected contrast.

ontology.mental_model: Introducing a contrastive or unexpected element.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'but' to signal a twist or an unexpected consequence.

positives: It was raining, but we still went out.
The car is old but reliable.
negatives: I want apples and oranges.
He is tall, so he plays basketball.

example_raw:
I really like my home, it is very small but it is very easy to clean. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Urdu; Pass)

I like my home, it's small but so comfortable, and the decoration is beautiful. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Portuguese; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use 'plus' to connect clauses and sentences, often to point out a positive addition or advantage.

ontology.mental_model: Adding a positive or advantageous clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Start a clause with 'plus' to add a bonus point or extra reason.

positives: It's a great hotel. Plus, it's very cheap.
We have lots of food, plus we ordered pizza.
negatives: Two plus two equals four.
The total is fifty plus tax.

example_raw:
I would be more than pleased to receive you at home, it's not too big, but we could have a lot of fun, plus you won't have to pay a thing! (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

It's around 200 so it's pretty cheap for a good game. Plus, it's really addictive and fun! (Philippines; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Tagalog; Pass)

It will be fun because everyone is going to be there. Plus, the park is the best place for a picnic, we can run and just have fun! (Philippines; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Tagalog; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use a range of conjunctions ('and, but, or, so, then') to combine more complex strings of clauses and sentences.

ontology.mental_model: Stringing multiple clauses together to narrate complex sequences.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use a variety of linkers to tell a continuous, multi-step story.

positives: I was tired so I went to bed, but I couldn't sleep.
He stood up and left the room, then the phone rang.
negatives: The cat and the dog.
Either yes or no.

example_raw:
I was scared and closed the window, but I couldn't sleep, so a few minutes later I opened the window again, but they were gone. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

Then we went to his limousine and we went to his studio and he was singing "Thriller" then I heard a strange voice, I woke up, and there was my mom waking me up. (Colombia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use 'plus' as coordinating conjunction, often in relation to numbers.

ontology.mental_model: Adding supplementary numerical or nominal entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'plus' to add an extra item or cost to a list.

positives: It costs five dollars plus tax.
My parents will come, plus my two brothers.
negatives: Plus, I don't really want to go.
It is a big advantage, plus it saves time.

example_raw:
In my house we are six people, my mother, my father, my sister and my two brothers, plus my two cats, which are members of the family too. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; ; Pass)

It cost me £2,500 plus the taxes. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

At the moment I pay 550 pounds monthly plus bills. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Spanish - European; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use 'both … and' to combine noun phrases, to give emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing the inclusion of two distinct nominal entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'both...and' to highlight that two things are equally involved.

positives: Both my mother and my father are doctors.
I have visited both Paris and London.
negatives: Both of them are coming.
I like apples and bananas.

example_raw:
I felt sorry for you because both friends and family are very important and having to pick one is very hard. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Turkish; Pass)

As a result of our aggressive and successful expansion strategy, both our market share and the number of our staff are increasing tremendously. (China; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Chinese; Fail)

Argentina has both wonderful country landscapes and excellent towns to enjoy. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

guideword: FORM/USE: 'BOTH … AND' WITH PHRASES AND CLAUSES
can_do_statement: Can use 'both … and' to combine phrases and clauses, often for emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing the inclusion of two distinct structural components (phrases/clauses).
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Apply 'both...and' not just to single words, but to whole phrases for stronger emphasis.

positives: They succeeded both at home and abroad.
The device can both entertain users and educate them.
negatives: Both the cat and dog slept.
I like them both.

example_raw:
And we have won a high reputation both at home and abroad. (China; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Chinese; Pass)

A lot of people think that television can both entertain and educate. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 2004; Italian; Pass)

Why not buying some extra beer and sell them on the beach? So, I could both get some enjoyment and make some money. So that was I did. (B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use 'neither … nor' to connect two words, phrases or clauses, often to give emphasis or focus.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing the exclusion of two alternatives.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'neither...nor' to strongly state that not one, and not the other, is true.

positives: Neither John nor Mary knew the answer.
We can neither eat nor drink in the library.
negatives: Neither of us wanted to go.
I don't know, nor do I care.

example_raw:
Neither you nor I would like that. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

We can neither eat nor drink during the lessons. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Polish; Pass)

I have neither climbed nor surfed before, so that would be very exciting for me. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Swedish; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use 'Neither' or 'Nor' + inverted auxiliary or 'be' + subject to add to a previous related negative clause, to focus on an additional negative factor.

ontology.mental_model: Appending a structurally inverted negative extension to a prior negation.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Follow a negative sentence with 'Neither' or 'Nor', then flip the subject and auxiliary to add another negative.

positives: I did not see the movie. Neither did my friend.
He is not ready. Nor is she.
negatives: Neither John nor Mary was there.
I like neither of them.

example_raw:
Nevertheless, I have no recollection of ever leaving my diary. In fact, I can clearly remember that I kept it with me all the time I was working. Neither do I remember losing it during the time I was on the platform waiting for my train to pull in. (Spain; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Catalan; Pass)

Maybe he will eventually get over this terrible experience, but he's bound to be a lonelier boy than he was. Nor does Jack's future look any more promising. (Italy; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Italian; Pass)

There are also considerable disturbances during day-time. It is, for example, not possible to lead a conversation, e.g. on the veranda, without shouting. Nor is it possible to watch television peacefully without the thunderous noise in the background. (Germany; C2 MASTERY; 1993; German; Pass)

At first, I didn’t pay attention to the large number of magazines and newspapers she subscribed to. Neither did I oppose her 'need' to get new clothes every month. (Spain; C2 MASTERY; 1998; Catalan; Pass)

can_do_statement: Can use 'either … or' to combine more complex strings of clauses and sentences.

ontology.mental_model: Framing an exclusive choice between complex alternative scenarios.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'either...or' to present two entirely different complex options or plans.

positives: Either we leave for the station right now, or we will miss the last train home.
You can either stay here and wait for her, or you can go ahead and I will join you.
negatives: Either the blue one or the red one.
I don't want either.

example_raw: And finally, about the present, you have two options; either you get something typical from your country, which they may like because you know how much they like collecting things from all over the world, or I get something from the wedding list store and sent it to them with your name on it and we can sort it out when you arrive here. (Spain; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1998; Catalan; Pass)
